# External MCP Server Catalog - Sweep Log, November 1-15, 2026

Archive for November 1-15, 2026. Discovery passes appear newest first. The [current sweep log](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/changelog) carries the most recent passes.

Archive: [October 16-31, 2026](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/changelog-2026-10b)

## 🆕 November 12, 2026 - Midday Sweep (1 New, 1 Guide)

Fired on the **10:00 MST** tick, seven hours after the night pass shipped four. The canonical came back set identical to that pass's capture (**64,577** raw entries against **64,573**, **20,885** distinct keys on both, **0 additions** and **0 removals**, the whole of the movement being four re-served entries in `servers/11`), so the window was the feed and the queue once more. The one entry that ships earned it on behaviour rather than on size.

- [Kuotia MCP - Spanish Autónomo Tax, Dated and Sourced](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/kuotia-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://kuotia.com/mcp`, no session, keyless for the four public tools, `initialize` **200** as `Kuotia` **1.0.1** on protocol `2025-06-18`, registry `com.kuotia/kuotia` **1.0.1**. **Nine** tools, each declaring its own `securitySchemes`: four public read-only, four reading a gestoría client's own record behind `kuotia:gestoria:read`, and one write annotated `destructiveHint: true` that sends only text the client approved with an `idempotency_key`. **Eight calls were driven**, and the finding is the refusal: modelo 303 for `2026-T3` returned a verified **deadline of 2026-10-20** with its direct-debit cutoff and an AEAT source, while the same modelo for `2026-T4` returned `isError: true` with code **`not_verified`**, the statutory window "del 1 al 30 de enero del año siguiente" and the IVA law as its source rather than presenting the general rule as the checked date. The estimators were driven to a **reproduced control**: 30,000 income with 5,000 expenses in Madrid returned **4,570.56** in contributions, **2,775.29** in IRPF and **17,654.15** net, the vendor's own published figures for the same example to the cent, and the RETA call returned tramo **5** between **380.88** and **639.45** as the vendor states. The connected half was measured to its gate instead of driven, and that gate is the mechanic worth knowing: a connected tool called without a connection answers **HTTP 200** with `isError: true` and `_meta["mcp/www_authenticate"]` carrying `error="insufficient_scope"`, `scope="kuotia:gestoria:read"` and the protected-resource pointer, so a client reading only the status code shows the operator nothing; the protected-resource document names one authorization server and two scopes and the RFC 8414 document publishes `authorization_code` plus `refresh_token`, `none` as the only client auth method and S256 only.

**Also identified this pass (not catalogued).** The closest call of the window is **Nock** (`com.usenock/nock` **1.0.0**, `https://api.usenock.com/mcp`), Brazilian B2B prospecting with buying signals, company and people search, enrichment and outreach: a keyless `initialize` answered **401** with `resource_metadata` and `scope="openid profile email"`, the protected-resource document named Clerk as the issuer, and the registry record described the product, so the evidence was there and the class was not - the lead-generation slice already carries Leadbay, Vibe Prospecting, VOYGR and Layrcake with AskBond and Skael held inside it, and Brazilian company data was held at **Fichário** on the regional CNPJ rule recorded against apipj, OpenBase, Corporary and Fuentio. **LaunchSpy** (`io.launchspy/launchspy` **1.2.0**, published the same day at 14:02Z) answered **401** with `missing_api_key` off a one-scope protected-resource document over coaches, course creators, their Meta ads, hooks and funnels, and holds on the ad-library class carried by Ad Library Intelligence, Adspy, SpyWinAds and the openadlibrary hold. From the queue, **Statuz**, **Felku Connect**, **HolicAudit**, **Cygnix SEO MCP**, **Dotmira**, **UTM Watch**, **VextCAD**, **YorkerAPI**, **garmlink**, **HappyKeywords**, **okdata**, **abap-config-mcp**, **TruthTrail**, **Sniptide**, **Crossdrive**, **while.sh**, **Rush**, **StatsPAI**, **Soko-kun**, **Pleso Therapy**, **Vidmoat**, **Roilo**, **SightRadar** and **Loop Marketing** were read and held on their class owners, each named in the sweep page. From the feed, **deltabridge** is threat intelligence, **remote-nomad-jobs** is the jobs class carried by roTEAMnet and the hiring entries, **ctlogs-dev** is certificate transparency in the class owned by the catalogued CTlogs.io, **alba-design** is a design utility, and **courio** and **quo** are recorded as unresolved rather than inferred: the mcp.so detail route answers "Only HTML requests are supported here" to a JSON-RPC probe and the reader proxy refused at **401** on bad IP reputation. **SealGuard**, **Aalto**, **Agent Demand Registry**, **volatiai** and the **mambalabsdev** fleet carry their previous dispositions.

## 🆕 November 12, 2026 - Night Sweep (4 New, 4 Guides)

Fired on the **03:00 MST** tick, six hours after the night pass. The canonical surface was flat in a way that can be checked rather than asserted - **three** raw entries more, **zero** distinct keys, **zero** stamps after the cut-off - so the whole window came from the mcp.so feed and the submission queue. All four entries answer a question an operator asks with a spreadsheet, a login or a phone call.

- [Vetto MCP - Fake Signup Checks Before the Account](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/vetto-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://usevetto.com/mcp`, keyless, `initialize` **200** as `vetto` **1.0.0** on protocol `2025-03-26`, **four** tools all annotated `readOnlyHint: true`, no official registry record found under the name (the search returns a different product). **Six calls were driven.** `check_email` on `jdoe@gmail.co` returned **BLOCK** with `reasons: ["typo", "dead"]` and the suggestion `jdoe@gmail.com`, so an assistant can rescue the customer inside the form; `billing@mailinator.com` returned **BLOCK** for `role` and `disposable` while `team+1@googlemail.com` returned **ALLOW** with `freemail` and `role` - **a role address alone does not block**, which is the ranking that keeps a real team inbox out of the bin; `same_inbox` proved `john.doe+promo@gmail.com` and `johndoe@googlemail.com` are one inbox and kept the control pair apart; `check_domains` on four domains answered `checked: 4, flagged: 2`; and `how_to_block` returned a server-side recipe that tells the caller to **fail open on timeout**, with the vendor's own 6.2x trial-abuse claim sourced to Stripe and its 800 ms fail-open stated on the page. First signup-integrity entry here.
- [Haven Financing MCP - Borrowing Against a Portfolio](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/haven-financing-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://app.haven.finance/api/mcp`, keyless, `haven-financing` **1.0.0**, registry `finance.haven/financing` **1.0.0**, **six** tools all read-only, four of them driven. A **1,000,000** collateral value and a **200,000** draw on the 12-month term priced to **9,700.20** financing interest plus a **900** fee, **10,600.20** all-in against **17,000** at 8.5 percent, so **6,399.80** saved a year; the same answer carried LTV **20 percent**, a **70 percent** facility cap, a **50,000** minimum draw and `collateralRequiredForDraw: 285,715`, with the assumptions printed rather than implied. `compare_existing_debt` priced all five options at once, the monthly variable line saving the most (**7,540.40**) and being the only one with no rate lock. **The finding is freshness:** the rate sheet's `asOf` is **2026-11-03T20:50Z**, nine days before the probe, and its rates sit 5 to 18 basis points below the table embedded in the vendor's own page on the day of reading, so the `asOf` field is the part to quote. First lending entry here.
- [SplitScanner MCP - Reverse Splits With the Filing Attached](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/splitscanner-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.splitscanner.com/mcp`, the **discovery-open, execution-gated** tier: a keyless `initialize` answered **200** as `splitscanner-mcp` **0.20.0**, a keyless `tools/list` answered **200** with exactly **24** tools all annotated read-only, and `tools/call` answered **401** JSON-RPC `-32001 Authentication required` without an OAuth discovery header, so the subscription boundary is measured and the answers are the vendor's. The tool surface is the argument: split history, lifecycle from proposal to effect, ended and abandoned splits, post-split performance, an **authority** query with `minRemaining` and `expiringBefore` for unused split authority, exchange listing standards, and SEC filing search with document, exhibit and in-text search beside it - every row cited to the filing or notice behind it. Registry `com.splitscanner/mcp` carries **0.19.0** and **0.19.1** against the **0.20.0** served, and the vendor's limits are quoted as given: scheduled is not confirmed, a missing value is not measured.
- [Tracwell MCP - Analytics Answered Inside the Chat](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/tracwell-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://tracwell.app/mcp`, measured at the **OAuth tier**: a keyless `initialize` answered **401** with `resource_metadata`, the protected-resource document named one authorization server and exactly **four** scopes (`analytics:read`, `definitions:write`, `websites:write`, `offline_access`), and the authorization-server document published dynamic registration, `code` as the only response type, `authorization_code` with `refresh_token`, `none` among the token auth methods and **`S256` only** - so reading analytics is one scope and the two write scopes touch goal and funnel definitions and site configuration, never the event stream. Registry `app.tracwell/analytics` **1.0.0**. The vendor documents the operator controls - **only workspace owners approve** a connection, the approval names **which websites** it can see, connections are revoked in Settings, and **all MCP access needs an active plan including trials** while expired plans keep the dashboard history - and its published plan ladder runs **9** to **149** USD a month with **API and MCP access included at every allowance**, which is the line worth having. Tool names are vendor statements and labelled as such.

**Also identified this pass (not catalogued).** **Diffbot** (`io.github.diffbot/diffbot-mcp`, `https://mcp.diffbot.com/mcp`) is the strongest vendor of the window and is held on its gate rather than on its merit: tool use needs a free Diffbot token, and no free token was provisioned for this pass, so nothing could be measured beyond the submission itself - it is the first target of the next pass with a token. **SealGuard** (`io.github.2cstudiodev-web/sealguard`, Solana wallet check-up with a 0-100 safety score) is consumer wallet hygiene, held on the crypto-safety class carried by the x402 and agent-security group. **FacturX** (`com.facturxapi/mcp`, Factur-X and ZUGFeRD validation against EN 16931 and the French 2026 rules) is held on the e-invoicing class carried by [NormAPI](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/normapi-mcp/), [BeeL](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/beel-mcp/) and Eleata, and it needs a sandbox key in any case. **Toolbox POD** (print-on-demand apparel, OAuth with dynamic client registration) and **Aalto** (an FF&E product library for interior design studios, OAuth with no keyless surface) are both real products that could not be measured past the handshake this pass and are held for a driven session rather than dismissed. **Deal.ai** is held on the consumer price-comparison class carried by Prickelly, CheapestInIndia and within; **OpenCheap** (one API across 900+ models) on the model-routing infrastructure class; **Agent Demand Registry** as a tool directory rather than a data surface; **Switchyard** and **agents-room** on the agent-gateway and agent-social classes; **Cred402** on the x402 credential class; **Scribase Mail** and **Sendblue** on the saturated messaging class; **SovaTalk**, **What's On Vegas** and **What's On Miami** on local events; **Neuro-CanvasLMS** on education; **Dagon Inference**, **fxapis MetaTrader 5** and **Safe Web Reader** by class; **volatiai-mcp** and submission **#7176** as empty submissions with no description or tools. The five `mambalabsdev` entries (**#7181** to **#7185**: Semrush domain metrics, YouTube channel email finder, property-owner records, Ticketmaster event prices, Eventbrite events) are the fourth wave of a fleet now **43** across four waves, held on the standing Apify-actor ruling. From the feed: **billdog-io** (paywalls, subscriptions and entitlements, OAuth-gated at `https://api.billdog.io/mcp` with protected-resource metadata) is held for a driven session; **twinr** (website to iOS and Android apps, 14 tools) on the app-builder class; **trainrec** as a consumer workout log; **internal-ballistics-calculator** as a hobby calculator; **lampwick** on developer monitoring; **mentionbird** on the AI-visibility class; **site-audit-mcp-server** and **seller-labs-amazon** on the Apify and Amazon-seller classes; **glen** on agent memory; **verrow** on parcel and zoning data; **farside-research** on crypto data; **blog-automation**, **glypse**, **mokxi**, **ctrl-cv**, **rentadriver** and **align-cli** by class; and the unstamped rail card set (`playwright-mcp`, `figma-context-mcp`, `github-mcp-server`, `pixellab-mcp`, `next-devtools-mcp`, `blockbench-mcp-plugin`, `supabase-mcp`) as catalogue furniture rather than arrivals.

## 🆕 November 12, 2026 - Midday Supplement Sweep (2 New, 2 Guides)

Fired on the **11:00 MST** tick, one hour after the midday pass shipped Kuotia. The canonical was flat to the key and not flat to the stamp - **thirteen** listings were re-indexed inside the hour and **not one of them is a new product** - so both entries that ship came from the mcp.so feed, and both are OAuth services with an operator-facing control surface rather than another reporting dashboard.

- [Hank MCP - Who Is On Call, Answered From the Chat](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/hank-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://app.dialhank.com/api/mcp`, registry `com.dialhank/hank` **1.0.0**. A keyless `initialize` answered **401** with `resource_metadata`; the protected-resource document named **two** scopes, **`hank.settings.read`** and **`hank.settings.write`**, and the RFC 8414 document published a **registration endpoint**, `code` as the only response type, `authorization_code` plus `refresh_token`, `none` as the only token auth method and **`S256`** only. The product is an AI receptionist for restoration and home-service companies and the tools edit the thing that actually decides whether an emergency call reaches anyone: the **on-call rotation**, transfer routes and their calling orders, office hours and holiday closures, service-area ZIP codes and the lead policy - **40** tools in the vendor's reference, led by `explain_call_routing`, `plan_routing_change` and `apply_routing_change`, where a plan **expires**, is bound to the user, app, organization, location and environment that made it, and `apply_routing_change` **refuses expired, changed, differently scoped or unauthorized plans** and returns the recorded result on a repeat. The permissions page states the operator controls plainly: the assistant holds your role, office hours and lead policy are Admin and Owner only, removals preview first, changes that would leave a routing gap are refused, the audit log records every action **without the values**, and a read-only connection still reads transcripts through `search_calls`. No account exists here, so the 40 tools are the vendor's documentation and the page says so.
- [RushCRM MCP - The WhatsApp Pipeline an Assistant Can Enter](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/rushcrm-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://rushcrm.com.br/api/v1/mcp/<account-slug>`, registry `br.com.rushcrm/crm` **1.0.0** declaring the `{slug}` template while the directory card prints one concrete org path. The keyless probe answered **401** with `resource_metadata` beside a **100 requests** rate-limit header and Cloudflare in front. The protected-resource document named **three** scopes in Portuguese - **`leitura`**, **`escrita`**, **`exclusao`** - and the authorization-server document published `/oauth/autorizar`, `/api/v1/oauth/token`, a registration endpoint, `/api/v1/oauth/revoke`, `code` only, `authorization_code` with `refresh_token`, `S256` only and `none` as the token auth method. The product is a Brazilian WhatsApp CRM and the vendor's README publishes **36** tools across contacts, deals and pipelines, activity, WhatsApp conversations, tags and forms, team targets and automations. Three details earn the guide: **`exclusao` is a separate scope from `escrita`**, so an assistant asked to keep the pipeline tidy never needs deletion rights; **the account administrator switches each tool on or off** in Settings → API → MCP Server, so the surface is per-connection rather than per-plan; and the automation group ships **`automacao_validar`** and **`automacao_simular`** beside create and update, the same plan-then-apply shape one layer up. Access tokens last **one hour**, the refresh token rotates on each use, and sending passes the CRM's own pacing protections. Published BRL pricing puts **API and MCP as a row in the plan comparison rather than an add-on**: 300 calls an hour on Starter at R$ 208 a month, 1,000 on Growth at R$ 348, 5,000 on Scale at R$ 698 and 5,000 on Enterprise from R$ 1,997.

**Also identified this pass (not catalogued).** The thirteen re-stamped listings were triaged rather than skipped, because a stamp says a page moved and not that a product arrived. **`heygen-com/hyperframes`** (**83,326** stars, *write HTML, render video*) is the largest repository touched in the hour and is **not an MCP server** - its README ships a CLI plus agent skills and names no MCP endpoint - so it belongs to the skills catalog and is recorded that way rather than stretched into the wrong page. **`wlsdks/ontology-atlas`** (**154** stars, a shared Markdown ontology of what a codebase builds and what a change could affect) is held on the codebase-comprehension class this catalog leaves to developer tooling and the agent-skill entries. **`jgravelle/jcodemunch-mcp`** (**2,843** stars, symbol-level code retrieval), **`daghis/teamcity-mcp`** (**32** stars, TeamCity builds and agents), **`tencentcloudbase/cloudbase-ai-toolkit`** (**1,165** stars, CloudBase backend for coding agents) and **`1mcp-app/agent`** (**530** stars, an MCP aggregator) are developer infrastructure with classes already covered here. **`eiry16/beacon-mfg`** (**2** stars, a bilingual directory of 210,000 Chinese businesses) is a company-data surface with a thin repository and no documentation trail. **`lakshmanturlapati/fsb`** (**204** stars, DOM-first browser automation, now redirecting to `fullselfbrowsing/FSB`) sits on the browser-automation class already carried. **`www-regdatalab-com-mcp`** has no resolvable repository under that name and is recorded **unresolved rather than inferred**. **`enkiduhub/mentionforge`** (1 star, agent-native social listening at $0.02 USDC per call with ten free trials) holds on the social-listening class and on its own evidence - a one-star repository is not a vendor yet. **`mambalabsdev/mcp-reddit-search-thread-scraper`** is the fifth wave of the one-tool-per-actor fleet now **44** across five waves under the standing Apify-actor ruling, and **`mediar-ai/screenpipe`** and **`n24q02m/notion`** describe surfaces already catalogued, where a re-stamp does not re-open a disposition. From the queue, **phonedriver** (#7220), **Magic Translate** (#7221), **Headshot Photo Check** (#7222) and **Louis Studios** (#7223) are two single-purpose utilities, one image compliance check and one design asset surface - none answers a business-operations question this catalog does not already cover. Nock, LaunchSpy, SealGuard, Aalto, Agent Demand Registry, Toolbox POD, FacturX, Deal.ai, OpenCheap, Switchyard, agents-room, Cred402, Scribase Mail, Sendblue, SovaTalk, the two What's On city servers, Neuro-CanvasLMS, Dagon Inference, fxapis MetaTrader 5, Safe Web Reader and volatiai carry the midday pass's dispositions, and **alba-design**, **courio** and **quo** remain unresolved for the same measured reason: the mcp.so detail route answers "Only HTML requests are supported here" to a JSON-RPC probe and the reader proxy refused at **401** on bad IP reputation.

## 🆕 November 12, 2026 - Evening Sweep (1 New, 1 Guide)

Fired on the **21:00 MST** tick, nine and a half hours after the midday supplement closed. The canonical gained **no key at all** in that window - the only movement was on the losing side - so the surface that carried the delta was the feed and the submission queue once more. The one entry that ships answers a question with arithmetic and then refuses to answer it when Google's own notices make the inputs untrustworthy.

- [Click Decay MCP - CTR Math That Refuses a Number](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/click-decay-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://clickdecay.com/mcp`, plain JSON, no session, **keyless**, `initialize` **200** as `clickdecay` **1.0.0** on protocol `2025-06-18` with `tools` as the only capability, registry `com.clickdecay/mcp-server` **1.0.0** active (published 2026-11-12T23:10:41Z), MIT, vendor QQQ OU in Tallinn, about **60** requests a minute per connection. **Four** tools, every one annotated `readOnlyHint: true` and `idempotentHint: true`. **Eleven calls were driven** and the arithmetic was re-done by hand as a control: 3,000 clicks from 100,000 impressions against 3,150 from 125,000 over two 28-day periods returned `clicksAtPriorCtr` **3,750** `modelled`, an impressions component of **+750** `calculated`, a CTR component of **-600** `calculated` and an observed click delta of **+150**, and the two components add back to the delta. The finding is the refusal: Google's impressions-logging anomaly runs **2025-05-13** to **2026-04-27**, and a comparison touching it returned `value: null` with `nullReason: "GSC_REPORTING_ANOMALY"` on every impressions-dependent figure - both CTRs, the impression delta, the percentage-point change, the relative change, both modelled figures and both components - while `clickDelta` stayed **+200** `observed` and the anomaly was listed with Google's own `sourceUrl`. `check_gsc_reporting_issues` returns the registry behind that behaviour, **two** records with their effects (`block_ctr_diagnostics` and `warn`). Three bad inputs were refused with machine-readable codes (`PERIOD_LENGTH_MISMATCH`, `PERIOD_OVERLAP`, `CLICKS_GT_IMPRESSIONS`); the defect recorded in the guide is that those refusals arrive as HTTP **200** with `structuredContent.errors` and no `content` block, so a client rendering only `content` shows nothing, and two observed figures come back unrounded.

**Also identified this pass (not catalogued).** Twenty-two queue arrivals and five feed cards were read and triaged, and the class owners are named so the next pass does not re-open them blind. **porter-metrics** (hosted marketing data, **45** tools, sign-in) is a real operator surface that holds on the marketing-data class carried by **Otto MCP**, **Manifold MCP** and **Metrinel**, with the semantic-layer owners **Dataddo**, **Catalogian** and **Azquo** one layer below. **lobbystack** is an open-source AI receptionist for calls, texts and appointments - the class **Hank MCP** entered this morning. **busabase** (MIT database and workspace shared by agents and people) is the agent system-of-record class, and **hms-x402** is x402 paid data origins in the class owned by **Cred402**. **textforagents** is a prior disposition, the pay-per-check publisher family. **Traxure** (release liveness for music catalogues) was measured to its gate - a keyless `initialize` answered **401** with `resource_metadata` and `scope="traxure"` - and holds on the catalogue class owned by **[DropCue MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/dropcue-mcp)**. **App Reviews**, **Competitor Ads** and **Shopify App Store Search** were filed within one second of each other by one publisher and scoped to its own Apify Actors, which is the standing Apify-actor ruling. **MexicoAPI** is official Mexican reference data with per-answer sources, and its validators (RFC, CURP, CLABE, NSS) are already covered by the catalogued **tlaloc-mcp-server**. **OpenRecord** (Epic MyChart portals, **50+** tools, local desktop extension) holds on the patient-chart class the **last-ehr** disposition set; **GlucoBeat** and **Hoy Planes** are consumer surfaces in carried classes; **AgentDrives** and **Fourth Feed** are tool directories, the **Agent Demand Registry** precedent; **Agent Guild** is a local install whose name collides with a June reputation-layer entry; **Browz**, **bootkey**, **SynapseOrch** and **FigmaMCP** each sit on browser automation, agent hosting, workflow automation and design tooling; **Alerta Chart**, **Bitcompare** and **ResultsZA** on markets and consumer gambling; **Geloky** on geocoding; **Construct** on 3D and CAD validation, where **VextCAD** was held; **PokerData** on hobby solvers.

## 🆕 November 11, 2026 - Night (1 New, 1 Guide)

Fired on the **21:00 MST** tick, ten hours after the midday supplement. The window is the largest of the day by raw entry count and the smallest by product count: **234** entries landed in `servers/11`, **181** of them inside a **96-second** bulk publish at **23:56Z**, and the feed offered a single fresh card. One product earned a guide, and it earned it by being driven rather than read.

- [Arcaeon MCP - An Agent Record That Cannot Be Quietly Rewritten](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/arcaeon-mcp/) - stdio Python server, `io.arcaeon/arcaeon` **0.10.0**, MIT, published **2026-11-11T17:16:40Z**, installed with `uvx --from arcaeon --with "mcp>=2.0.0,<3" arcaeon mcp`, `initialize` **200** as `arcaeon` **0.10.0** on protocol `2025-06-18` with **19** tools listed, **17** free and two paid (`witness_pin`, `witness_renew`) behind `ARCAEON_KEY`. It is the consolidation of thirteen packages into one and the registry records the migration, with `io.arcaeon/adapter` now **deprecated** under the message `Merged into io.arcaeon/arcaeon`. **Eleven calls were driven in one session and three carry the argument.** Two records appended and verified as `rows: 2, chained: 2, breaks: 0`, then one word changed in row one outside the server (`weather` to `sunshine`), which `ledger_verify` answered as `ok: false` with `first_break: "line 1: chain mismatch"` before a restore returned `ok: true`; the same response carries a `calls_record` block, a second hash-chained ledger of the MCP calls the server served, so hiding a served call means breaking two chains. `vet_grade` on one of this profile's own Python MCP servers returned `source_sha256` `a8bdaba8…`, **nine** checks and two findings: `unsafe-exec` **high** at line 105 (`subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`) and `audit-record` **medium** at line 118, where presence and tamper-evidence passed while **completeness and reconstructability failed** on a missing tool name, timestamp and argument digest, and the artifact ships its own blind spots, including that the battery reads bytes and never sends them. A `deal_mandate` of `acme-supply` up to `500.00` USD, two commits written deliberately apart at `39.00` and `41.00`, and `deal_dispute` returned **ALTERED at commit#1** naming `mandate_digest` and `terms.total` with `counts: buyer 2, seller 1`, while `second_read_compare` on a missing ledger returned `COULD NOT LOOK` with exit **3** rather than a 0 percent agreement. **The limits are the vendor's own and unusually specific:** tamper-evident is not tamper-proof, the witness is operated by the same people who ship the package, the daily anchor is a clock and not a party, truncation is caught only by a pin, and neither truth nor authorship is proven. Writing costs about **18 ms** a row, so 102,000 rows took roughly 22 minutes, while a 50 MB log verifies in about 2.5 seconds. This is the second Arcaeon page here and it is not a duplicate: [arcaeon-ledger-mcp](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/arcaeon-ledger-mcp/) covers the standalone pip ledger as it stood in August, and this covers the consolidated package with the source grader, the evidence pack and the deal tape. It enters beside [AgentKeyGate](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/agentkeygate-mcp/) on the credential side and [AnythingMCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/anythingmcp/) on the gateway side, as the evidence trail rather than the door.

## 🆕 November 11, 2026 - Midday Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)

Fired on the **10:00 MST** tick, seven hours after the early-morning pass. The overnight window was flat to the entry count and took its finds from one publish batch; this window is the opposite, with **294** new server keys in the canonical that had to be decomposed before three products could be found. All three entries catalogue an operator question that a paper process answers badly: what a metal actually costs delivered, what an event date costs at the wrong hour, and what a client has still not confirmed.

- [Bullion Price Check MCP - Dealer Metal Pricing and Stock](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/bullion-price-check-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://bullionpricecheck.com/mcp`, registry `com.bullionpricecheck/bullion-price-check` with **2.0.0** published and **2.1.0** served, keyless throughout with **27** tools all annotated `readOnlyHint: true`. Six calls were driven. Spot read gold **4,002.80**, silver **52.38**, platinum **1,551** USD/ozt at a **76.42** ratio with a per-metal timestamp and a freshness block (`spot_age_minutes: 70` against **120**), and palladium declared out of scope in the response. The dealer ladder for one silver round ran **4.57 percent** over melt at the low to **20.59 percent** at the top, an **8.39 USD** spread, with three `Partner` labels ranked 2, 4 and 5 - live proof that a partner pays to list and never to rank - and two exclusions stated with reasons (out of stock; a price **471 minutes** old against a 60-minute source limit). The Premium Index shows the **median dealer at two to two and a half times the lowest premium** on the same five silver products. `true_cost` priced ten units delivered at **3,316.50 each** with a **1,120** card surcharge on top, and `bullion_sales_tax` answers per state with the rule text and **partial** and **taxable** statuses, not a binary flag. Eleven dealer tools cover stock aging, restock points, scrap intake and buyback spread. First bullion entry in this catalog.
- [TouristPads MCP - Singapore Event Rental Quotes](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/touristpads-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://touristpads.com/mcp`, registry `com.touristpads/touristpads` **1.0.0**, keyless, **three** tools with only `request_quote` a write. `list_rental_options` returned **16** products with quantity ceilings (**104** iPad 10.2 bodies, **22** routers, **3** iPhone 17s), four accessories and **ten** rules. A six-iPad two-router three-day order priced to **2,407.00 SGD** where equipment was **68.6 percent** and the calendar **31.4 percent** (delivery 106.80, after hours **150**, Sunday leg **500**), and the server then volunteered a Monday collection at **1,907.00 SGD**, exactly **500** less, with the initialize instructions telling the assistant to surface it. The published rules hold the levers an operator can pull: a **280 SGD** equipment minimum, **75 per 30 minutes** outside 9am to 6pm per leg, **500** for a Sunday or holiday leg, **8 percent off at 2,000** and **10 percent at 3,000** applied automatically, and location surcharges added at signing rather than quoted. The estimate says plainly that no quote has been issued, and an after-hours charge needs the customer's agreement first. First event-equipment rental entry here.
- [photoproof MCP - Client Proofing for Photographers](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/photoproof-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://photoproof.io/mcp`, registry `io.photoproof/mcp` **1.0.0**, recorded at the **OAuth evidence tier**: a keyless `initialize` answered **401** with `resource_metadata` and `scope="galleries:read galleries:write"`, and both metadata documents were read - one protected resource naming one authorization server, and an authorization-server document publishing dynamic registration, `code` as the only response type, `authorization_code` with `refresh_token`, `none` among the token auth methods and **`S256` only** for PKCE. Two scopes is the whole grant, so a reporting assistant can read galleries and cannot create one. The product is proofing rather than selling: a client opens one link, **selects, rejects or comments without an account** and presses **Confirm** to lock the selection, the selected codes paste into **Lightroom**, delivery takes finals **up to 4 GB per file**, and galleries carry a password, a watermark, a download lock and view tracking. ## 🆕 November 11, 2026 - Early Morning Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)

Fired on the **03:00 MST** tick, six hours after the evening sweep's read. The two surfaces disagreed and both readings are recorded: **mcpservers.org was flat to the entry count**, every one of its twelve server maps carrying exactly the URL count it carried at 21:00 MST, while the mcp.so feed delivered **one scheduled batch of eight cards** all stamped `2026-11-11T08:00Z`. Three of those eight earned guides, and all three are local-first tools that were installed and driven on this host rather than described from a README: an email archive converter, a security scanner for agent-written code, and a memory server whose statements can be corrected without being deleted.

- [dead-letter MCP - Email Archives an Agent Can Actually Read](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/dead-letter-mcp/) - local stdio, `uvx --python 3.12 --from "dead-letter[mcp]" dead-letter-mcp`, registry record `io.github.BigCactusLabs/dead-letter` **0.4.10**, protocol `2025-06-18`. `tools/list` returned exactly **five** tools (`convert_eml`, `convert_eml_to_bundle`, `convert_directory`, `convert_mbox`, `get_diagnostics`) with `get_diagnostics` the only one annotated `readOnlyHint: true`, and `resources/list` plus `prompts/list` returned **zero** entries although both capabilities are advertised. A crafted message with a duplicated plain-text part, an HTML signature table, a tracking pixel and `In-Reply-To` headers converted to **465** bytes of Markdown: one body rather than two, the signature preserved as a Markdown table, the date normalised to ISO 8601 UTC from a `-0500` header, and the tracking pixel **kept by default** until `--strip-tracking-pixels` was passed. `--strip-signatures` did **not** remove the table-shaped signature, which is the measured limit of a delimiter heuristic. The licence is the first decision, not the last: **PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0**, "any noncommercial purpose is a permitted purpose", no commercial licence published, so an internal company pipeline sits outside the grant. The vendor's own benchmark is labelled as such: roughly **88 percent** fewer tokens than raw `.eml` across an 11-message synthetic set, with the attachment category median about **126,000** tokens raw against **180** converted, and the README says plainly that naive extractors are cheaper because they discard metadata. There is no mailbox connection: it converts files you already exported, and the CLI accepts `.zip` and `.tgz` where the MCP tools do not.
- [Vibe Shield MCP - The Security Scan Before an Agent Says Done](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/vibe-shield-mcp/) - npm CLI plus MCP server, zero runtime dependencies, MIT, `@vibefoundry/vibe-shield` **2.1.2**, registry `io.github.avivgerz-hue/vibe-shield` **2.1.2**, repository created **2026-11-07** with 26 stars. On a crafted Next.js App Router route with four planted defects it returned **GRADE F, 0/100, 5 critical** in **26 ms** over **80** active rules: three unguarded mutation routes (`VSB-AUTH-001` twice), one concatenated SQL statement (`VSB-DB-007`), one record owner taken from the request body (`VSB-AUTH-004`), and one hardcoded credential (`VSB-SECRET-001`) that the report **redacted** as `sk_liv••••` rather than reprinting it. Exit codes were measured four ways: plain scan **1**, `--fail-on critical` **1**, `--format json` **1**, and a clean control file `GRADE A+` **0**. The JSON report carries `schemaVersion`, `attackSurface`, per-finding `cwe`, `owasp`, `confidence` and a `remediation` object with an insecure and a secure example, and the score object states its own cap: `{"ceiling":{"severity":"critical","limit":29}}`, so a single critical pins the maximum at **29**, which is why the agent-surface audit reported `GRADE F, 29/100`. That audit is the second command and the honest half of this entry: on a poisoned `SKILL.md` it caught the exfiltration (`VSB-AGENT-002`, a `curl` posting `env` to a remote host) and the missing manifest scope (`VSB-AGENT-010`) across **12** rules, and flagged **neither** "ignore all previous instructions" nor "never mention this section", so it detects what an instruction does, not what it asks a reader to hide. The vendor states its own limit on the demo: "a clean score is not a security guarantee."
- [CtxVault MCP - Memory You Correct Instead of Overwrite](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/ctxvault-mcp/) - local stdio server and CLI over the same vaults, MIT, package **0.9.1** on PyPI while `initialize` reports `ctxvault` **1.30.0**, registry `io.github.Filippo-Venturini/ctxvault` **0.9.1**, 62 stars, protocol `2025-06-18`. Memory is split into three vault types: semantic documents read by meaning, skill procedures read by name, and episodic statements holding two timelines, `valid_from`/`valid_to` in the world and `known_at` in the vault. `tools/list` returned **17** tools, more than the eleven the README names, and the episodic set is the design: `write_episode`, `query_episodes` (with `valid_at`, `known_at` and `include_closed`), `supersede_episode`, `invalidate_episode`, `revise_episode`, `confirm_episode`, `dispute_episodes`, `episode_history` and `list_entities`. The lifecycle was run on a throwaway vault: two statements about one customer, one from an invoice and one from a contract amendment, both stayed **open**, which is the first thing to know because an append corrects nothing by itself; `supersede` then closed the first at the exact microsecond the replacement opened, kept its source, recorded `superseded by` pointing at the new record, and deleted nothing. `dispute` leaves two contradictory statements open rather than picking a winner, which is closer to how an operator treats two sources that disagree. Storage is measured, not inferred: one directory per vault holding one `episodes.db`, with `restricted` and `allowed_agents` in the config, so isolation is a filesystem boundary. The cost is measured too: `uv tool install ctxvault` occupies **5.9 GB** because `sentence-transformers` and `chromadb` are hard dependencies that resolve PyTorch and the CUDA runtime wheels on Linux, and an episodic vault builds no vectors unless an embedding model is named at init. Not first of class here, but the first entry where the correction itself is a tool with a closing timestamp.

**Also identified this pass (not catalogued).** Five held, each on a measured reason rather than a preference. **caprock** (43 stars, Apache-2.0, Go and Tauri, no registry record) is an agentic development environment following every pull request to release with what the agents spent, held because it is a desktop application with a companion plugin rather than a server an assistant attaches to, and because its positioning names Gemini CLI among the four agents it hosts, which is outside the surfaces this documentation speaks to. **unslop** (20 stars, MIT, **72** rules across seven design pillars) holds as class-owned: [CoDesign](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/codesign-mcp/) carries the editable design engine and [Design Context Bridge](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/design-context-bridge-mcp) carries Figma-to-code, and it also carries a genuine registry collision worth recording, two different records under one product name (`io.github.0design/unslop` 0.1.0 and `io.github.avivgerz-hue/unslop` 2.1.1) where a search that stops at the first hit grades the wrong product. **usb-rea** (MIT, registry 0.2.1 and 0.3.0) reverse engineers a USB gadget from captured vendor traffic, held on audience: no entry in this catalog serves an operator through a USB bus. **tandoor-recipe-mcp** (MIT, registry 3.4.0 and 3.4.1, **306** tools, a `preview_*` sibling for every destructive delete) is the most carefully built server in the batch and still a household surface, with one detail recorded for anyone who disagrees, that it needs **Node 24** or later where this host runs Node 22. **agent-vscreen** (56 stars, MIT, Kotlin, no registry record) is a background virtual screen for Android agents working apps on an invisible display through Shizuku with no root, held because its endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:18765/mcp` on the device, so nothing about it is verifiable from a server; it is held rather than dismissed and a re-check needs an Android device, not another read.

## 🆕 November 10, 2026 - Evening Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)

Fired on the **21:00 MST** tick, ten hours after the midday supplement. The canonical grew by **fifteen** server URLs across the same fifteen-map index, the queue carried **twenty-nine** arrivals from **#7100** to **#7128**, and the feed carried **thirteen** cards above the 14:05Z cutoff. All three entries catalogued are day-of operating surfaces: a departure manifest, a patrol round, and an action ledger with an undo window.

- [TripWorks MCP - Tour Operator Bookings and Manifests](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/tripworks-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.tripworks.com/mcp`, registry record `com.tripworks/tripworks` **1.0.2** published **2026-11-08T23:14:34Z**, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic registration and `S256`-only PKCE. A keyless `POST initialize` answered **401** with a JSON-RPC error object (`-32001 Missing or malformed Authorization header`) and a `WWW-Authenticate` header naming its protected-resource path, which returned **200** and pointed at an authorization server on the same host. That metadata document publishes **fifty** scopes, and the set is the product brief: `bookings.read` and `bookings.write`, `manifest.read`, `waivers` and `waiver-types`, `experience-timeslots`, `gift-cards`, `promo-codes`, `resellers`, `reviews`, `payments.read`, `phone-calls.read`, `reports.read`, `audit-log.read` and `api-logs.read`, with the manifest, payments and the audit log read-only by construction. The vendor help article publishes the per-area permission map and three controls that stack: the connection runs as the person who approved it and never exceeds their permission group, the approval screen offers Read, Write or both with Write unchecked blocking every change, and every write returns a preview that must be confirmed. Its protocol boundary is the clearest recorded here: with MCP a person is behind the connection and each request needs their approval, while an API key or a Zapier connection is a standing credential nobody approves, so the vendor recommends MCP when a person is in the loop. Report links expire in **15 minutes**. First tour and activity operator entry in this catalog.
- [PatrolTech MCP - Guard Tours, Missed Rounds, Incidents](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/patroltech-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.patroltech.online/mcp`, registry record `online.patroltech/patroltech` **0.2.7** published **2026-11-01T04:52:20Z** with `/health` already serving **0.2.8**, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic registration and client ID metadata documents. A keyless `initialize` answered **401** with `error="invalid_token"`, `scope="read write"` and a `resource_metadata` path that answered **200** naming a separate authorization host, whose RFC 8414 document publishes `authorization_code`, `refresh_token`, `S256` only, `none` for token auth, a revocation endpoint, a JWKS and the issuer response parameter; the same document on the MCP host answers **404**, so only the protected-resource document connects the two hosts. Writes never land directly: `patroltech_<area>_propose_<verb>` queues a proposal, one user and client form one batch of at most **10** expiring after **30 minutes**, and `patroltech_proposals_confirm` runs it in order as proposed. Without the `write` scope writes answer **403 insufficient_scope**. The server holds no credentials and forwards the user's token, a closed list of writes is allowed to agents, and deleting records, inviting users and billing are outside its capability. Results are capped at **60,000** characters, reads at **60** calls a minute and writes at **20**, and every call writes one audit line holding a hash of the arguments and never the arguments. Four prompts and two resources carry the vocabulary, and the `reading-the-data` resource is the one that stops an assistant calling a rejected scan a missed round. First security patrol entry here.
- [Genaya MCP - A Service Business Workspace With Undo](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/genaya-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://api.genaya.com/mcp`, registry record `io.github.genaya-app/genaya` **1.2.0** published **2026-11-10T19:58:07Z**, hours before this pass. Discovery is open and execution is gated: a keyless `initialize` answered **200** as `genaya` 1.2.0, `tools/list` answered **200** with exactly **seven** tools, and an unauthenticated `tools/call` answered **401** with `scope="read ai act send offline_access"`. The seven are `ask_genaya`, `genaya_act`, `confirm_action`, `cancel_action`, `undo_action`, `list_actions` and `whoami`, which makes the assistant's own changes a readable object rather than an audit report to go looking for. The vendor's split is the product: a record change is confirmed in the chat and can be undone for **15 minutes**, while texts, emails and anything about money are confirmed on a Genaya page where the member is signed in. Both well-known documents answered **200** with the same five scopes, and the reference page states the per-host constraints for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Slack and Salesforce Agentforce plus the `gnc_` organization-issued clients that must present a secret. A `POST initialize` answered **401** with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=".../.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"` and `scope="openid profile email offline_access"`, and following that path returned the protected-resource document. The vendor documents **nine** tools on the current tool set and **eleven** on the earlier one, the difference being the legacy `describe_table` and `describe_tables` pair that `search_data_catalog` now covers: `get_data_context`, `get_account_health`, `search_docs`, `search_data_catalog`, `query_metrics`, `run_bigquery_sql`, `shopify_admin_graphql`, `meta_ads_query` and `submit_feedback`. The published order is the transferable part, `get_data_context` then `search_data_catalog` then `query_metrics` when a named metric matches, then describe and SQL only when it refuses, so the model cannot quietly substitute its own revenue definition for the workspace's. Limits are published as numbers (**500** warehouse rows before truncation, **100** Shopify and Meta records per page, **10 GiB** billed bytes per query, **60 s** and **30 s** query budgets, **256 KiB** per response), and the vendor documents Hermes by name with `hermes mcp add sourcemedium --url https://mcp.sourcemedium.com/mcp --auth oauth` and `hermes mcp test sourcemedium`. ## 🆕 November 8, 2026 - Midday Sweep (1 New, 1 Guide)

A keyless `initialize` answers **200** as `ListRiver` **0.1.0** on protocol `2025-06-18` and returns all three tool schemas plus the server's own instruction set; `tools/call` then returns the documented **401** naming `LISTRIVER_API_KEY`, so the surface is fully readable before a credential exists. Three tools: `list_states`, `count_businesses`, `search_businesses`. **The first two are free and the third spends records**, which is the whole reason the entry exists: every other business-data server in this catalogue makes you learn the size of a market by buying the pull, and here an agent sizes a market, narrows it on `has_phone`, `has_email`, `naics`, `entity_type` and `formed_within`, and only then retrieves names, with a cursor to continue rather than restart. Records are **filings, not profiles**: address, county, registered agent and formation month, plus phone, email, website, EIN and NAICS where the state publishes them, which makes **a business filed last month** a prospect with no website to audit and no ad history to bid against. Two limits come from the server itself and are recorded as the two ways this surface can mislead: phone, email, NAICS and county coverage is **partial and state-dependent**, and the server instructs the agent to check with `count_businesses` before promising a phone list; and the records carry a use restriction barring **credit, insurance, employment or housing** decisions, which is the FCRA boundary stated plainly. Free tier **500** records a calendar month, then **$50** for 5,000 rising to **$450** for 75,000, with prepaid packs and an AWS Marketplace path; the record is the unit and every re-returned business counts again. ## 🆕 November 8, 2026 - Evening Sweep (6 New, 6 Guides)

Fired on the **21:00 MST** tick, ten hours after the midday supplement, and the window was the largest of the day: **186** sitemap additions after two identical passes, **24** queue issues, and a scheduled bulk publish stamped four hours ahead of the clock. Six servers are catalogued, each on evidence rather than on a card. The wave itself decomposes once rather than one at a time: **19** Cotlet per-app connectors become one entry, **47** documentation-route slugs hold on the November 1 ruling, **12** BumiAtlas land-record datasets and **12** MambaLabs creator tools hold as single-publisher families, **8** x402 worker artifacts hold as worker artifacts, **3** MCPKit-RU Yandex tools hold on geography, and the **85** individual slugs were resolved through the official registry rather than guessed from domain-shaped names.

- [Vericto MCP - SQL Guardrails Before the Query Runs](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/vericto-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.vericto.com/mcp`, an OAuth account surface at `/mcp/account`, and a self-hosted proxy at `docker run vericto/vericto-proxy:5.0.0 mcp`, registry records `com.vericto/mcp`, `com.vericto/vericto-proxy` and `com.vericto/account`, filed as three submissions in the same second. A keyless `initialize` answers **401** naming the header it wants, so the tier is documented and gated rather than driven. **This is the first entry here that decides about a statement before it runs.** Rules are written on the parsed syntax tree rather than on query text, so a comment or a subquery cannot walk around them; columns are masked in the result; each agent gets its own table and column allowlist; a rule simulator tests a change against real traffic; policies roll out observe-before-enforce with a kill switch; and every decision lands in an audit trail with signed reports. The AGPL-3.0 proxy states its own behaviour and is the reason to trust the free tier: with no account it applies the built-in rules for destructive statements, a missing `WHERE`, risky DDL and data exposure, **reports nothing anywhere**, and runs every statement in a read-only transaction that ends in `ROLLBACK`, executing exactly what it checked. The same engine fails a deploy (`vericto check migrations/*.sql` returns `BLOCKED VERICTO-001 DELETE without WHERE` with a suggested fix). The class neighbour is [DutyKit](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/dutykit-mcp/) on the compliance side, and the distinction is that read-only access is a property of a credential while this is a policy with a receipt.
- [frag.hugo MCP - German GDPR Duties on a Calendar](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/frag-hugo-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.fraghugo.de/mcp`, registry `de.fraghugo/frag.hugo`, submission `#6957`, **14** tools on a keyless `tools/list` and OAuth for the **42** account tools. **Driven live twice.** `search_gdpr_fines` returned **101** cases with the newest three: Xandr, a Microsoft company, **EUR 8,600,000** from Datatilsynet for real-time bidding data that allowed inference about sexual orientation, IQVIA Solutions Italy at **EUR 7,000,000** from the Garante, and Google Ireland at **EUR 403,000,000** from the DPC, each with the articles, a summary and the regulator's own URL. `get_compliance_deadlines` returned **18** dated obligations from the day of the call, including the AI Act deepfake prohibition on **2026-12-02** under Art. 5(1)(ba) and (bb), the machine-readable labelling duty for systems already on the market the same day under Art. 50(2), and the product liability change on **2026-12-09** that makes software a product under Directive (EU) 2024/2853. Beyond the calendar: `get_subprocessor_changes` watches the subprocessor lists of **17** cloud providers, `find_supervisory_authority` resolves the competent German authority from a postcode, `get_cyber_threat_picture` counts ransomware leak-site naming by industry, `check_email_security` reads SPF, DKIM, DMARC, DNSSEC, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT, BIMI and CAA, `report_data_breach` starts the 72-hour Art. 33 clock and `create_data_subject_request` the one-month Art. 12 deadline. The guardrails are stated by the server: mail and deletion run preview-then-confirm, every change is undoable for **90 days**, and what is submitted is reviewed by a data protection officer. [ISMS Copilot](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/isms-copilot-mcp/) carries the certification programme and this is the dated reference registry beside it, in German, with its own boundary stated - no legal advice in an individual case.
- [Sentinelle Creances MCP - The Creditor Claim Deadline](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/sentinelle-creances-mcp/) - keyless Streamable HTTP at `https://creances.amacunia.fr/mcp`, server `Sentinelle creances FR` **1.30.0**, **2** tools, registry `io.github.Marcoco27/sentinelle-creances`, submission `#6956`. **Driven live.** `creances_example` returned SIREN **910759158**, a **liquidation judiciaire** opened by judgment on **2026-10-29**, published in the BODACC on **2026-11-08**, with `date_limite_declaration` **2027-01-08**, **60** days remaining, the forclusion register closing **2027-05-08**, the liquidator named from the judgment text and the bodacc.fr notice linked. `creances_lookup` then returned an **x402 version 2** payment requirement instead of an error: **0.01 USDC** on Base, no account, no key, `maxTimeoutSeconds` 300, with the legal rule in the resource description - two months from publication, four from abroad, article R622-24 of the code de commerce, one to fifty SIREN or SIRET per call. This is the first entry here where a business fact costs a cent and pays through a wallet, and the honest limitation is that a finance team without one cannot use it. French company data already has owners - [OpenBase](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/openbase-mcp/) serves **20.5M** entities with BODACC proceedings - and what neither it nor Corporary does is the procedure: which judgment opened a window, which publication starts the clock, what the last day is, and when the claim is struck. The sibling `catnat.amacunia.fr` applies the same instrument to natural-disaster decrees and the 30-day insurance window, recorded in the guide rather than as a seventh entry.
- [DSers MCP - The Dropshipping Loop Behind a Chat](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/dsers-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://ai.dsers.com/mcp/mcp-so`, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE only, **no API keys**, from the vendor itself. A keyless `initialize` answers **401** with `invalid_request`, an MCP protocol version of **2025-11-25** that is newer than most of this catalogue, a correlation id for support, and both metadata documents published. Those documents are the product brief: **23 scopes** that describe the loop exactly - `supplier:read` to find a supplier product, `product:import`, `product:mapping` and `product:push` to publish it, `order:write` to place the supplier order, `tracking:read` to read what comes back, beside store, staff, theme, settings and billing scopes. - [Cotlet MCP - The Apps That Have No API](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/cotlet-mcp/) - the architecture of the window, and the reason **19** sitemap slugs became one entry. Remote Streamable HTTP at `https://cotlet.dev/mcp/v1` with **719** tools, and at `https://cotlet.dev/mcp/v1/<app>` per app, where Fresha returns **42**; registry records under `dev.cotlet`. A keyless `initialize` answers **200** and returns an instruction block that is a safety contract: Cotlet runs the user's own Chrome in the cloud, **the user signs in themselves**, passwords are never asked for and never typed, and on a sign-in page, a two-factor prompt or a step that needs a person the agent must stop and hand over the browser link. The typed half is a working front desk per app, every integration a `_read` and `_write` pair with the operation in `operation` and its inputs in `arguments`: Fresha carries list and create appointment, reschedule, cancel, add client, reply to review; Skool carries **30** read and **41** write operations; Tradify **11** and **12**. The apps are the ones a service business actually runs and that have no API: salons and spas, cleaning and field service, contractors, photography studios, auto shops, restaurants, property managers, plus CRM, HR and e-signature. Where no typed tool exists, **25** browser tools take over, reading a page as numbered elements. Three governance decisions make it usable: writes that reach other people return `pending` with a `call_id` and wait for approval in the Cotlet console, `cotlet_whoami`, `cotlet_apps` and `cotlet_balance` are free so an assistant can report before it spends, and automations are scripted jobs that run with no model and test with every write skipped. Cost is credits and per-minute browser time, the typed coverage is only what Cotlet has written, and the browser path inherits the fragility of every web UI.

**Also identified this evening (not catalogued).** `supercatch-com-ai` answered keylessly with **82** tools, prepare and execute pairs for every write and idempotency keys on every mutation, held on the collectible pricing class where the PokéInvest ruling stands, with the reversal test recorded as a store-operations question rather than a price question; `pokeitem/pokeitem-mcp` on the same class; `oort`, `memscope-ai`, `ragionex/memory-mcp`, `nkoteskey/constellate` and `nifetency/mcp-excel` on memory, workspace and spreadsheet classes; `saifuban` as an agent spend guard and `mishmar-io/mishmar` as trading risk control; `screenata/screenata-mcp` on the compliance programme class carried by ISMS Copilot; `voxisim/voxisim-mcp` on phone numbers; `anyhook/anyhook` on developer infrastructure; `aurelix-solutions/aurelix-mcp` and `apinoahq/apinoa-mcp` on the Apify-actor hold; `findbroadband/mcp`, `patternswizard-com-open-data`, `tokenmark-mcp`, `perigee`, `microlaunch-mcp`, `agent-company-mcp`, `flisk`, `spcn-usa/specialneeds-cli`, `liquid-composer`, `newsjack-cc-mcp`, `seencxy/solvehub-mcp` and `jumpermcp/jumper-publisher` outside operator scope or on a class this catalogue owns; `cloro-dev/mcp-server` as the August 12 `cloro` entry re-listed under a new slug; from the queue, `hiveref` on hiring verification beside FoundRole, `nod` as a local approval primitive beside DutyKit, `otdeck` and `kafdesk` as desktop-bundled local servers, `annsa` on project management, `boterly`, `gameye`, `memorybrain`, `yandex-tracker-mcp-lite`, `virtnumber`, `fwrd-sms-mcp`, `agent-vscreen`, `favicondl`, `qsignals`, `saascustomdomains`, `clockintoday` on the jobs class and `pokeitem` on retail; and the **47** documentation-route slugs plus the BumiAtlas, MambaLabs, x402-worker and MCPKit-RU families as listed in the sweep report.

Both are catalogued, and the first is catalogued for the direction of its delegation rather than its category.

- [Marsell MCP - The AI Marketer That Hires Your Agent](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/marsell-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://getmarsell.com/mcp`, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE or a Bearer `mk_` agent key, registry record `com.getmarsell/marsell` active since `2026-11-04T00:08:52Z`. A keyless `initialize` answers **200** as `marsell` **1.0.0** on protocol `2025-06-18` and returns an instruction block that reads as an operating manual; `tools/list` returns all **126** tools with schemas and annotations; `tools/call` returns the documented **401** naming the agent key. **The finding is the direction of the delegation.** Every other marketing entry in this catalogue is a tool the assistant calls; Marsell is a client that calls the assistant back. `homework_list` queues the jobs the platform cannot do because they need the owner's own logins, files or inbox, and `homework_done` is **verified by the platform itself** for jobs it can confirm. `missions_next` returns one message at a time to be sent word for word from the owner's own signed-in browser, and a refused mission is recorded rather than reworded. `get_brand` holds what the business is while `owner_fact_set` writes the owner's corrections, which every plan, post and page reads first. Money is quoted before it is spent: `picture_price`, `series_quote`, `business_read_quote` and `get_tokens` all price the work ahead of the render, and the server tells the assistant to say what it costs. The setup is a scripted conversation (`get_setup`, `fill_setup`, `set_offer`, `set_preferences`, `finish_setup`) that refuses to close until the owner's goal, one number and one date are recorded; connecting the accounts and pressing Start are reserved to the owner by instruction. Plans run **$49** a month for 200,000 tokens to **$799** for 3,600,000, annual at ten times monthly, extra tokens from **$1.80** down to **$1.50** per 10,000, with ad spend and creator fees separate. Documented rather than driven, and the backend is private, both recorded as limits. The class it enters is crowded ([Toffu](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/toffu-mcp/) on ads, [Maeve Social](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/maeve-social-mcp/) on publishing, [CampaignStack](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/campaignstack-mcp/) on outreach, [Layers Growth](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/layers-marketing-mcp/) on one channel) and none of them dispatches work back to the user's own agent.
- [Worth Leaving MCP - Walk-Away Math for Unvested Equity](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/worth-leaving-mcp/) - keyless Streamable HTTP at `https://worthleaving.com/api/mcp`, no account, per-IP rate limit, no inputs stored, registry record `com.worthleaving/verdict` **1.1.0** published `2026-11-08T17:38:20Z`, four minutes before the submission was filed. `initialize` **200** as `worth-leaving` **1.1.0**; **one** tool, `compute_walk_away_verdict`, read-only and idempotent. **The instruction is the entry:** never compute vest dates or dollar totals yourself. Driven live with a two-grant scenario it returned `take-it` at **77/100**, a walk-away cost of **$62,500**, an offer threshold of **$230,000** a year before tax, an annual net gain of **$28,965** and a next vest on **2027-02-01** worth **$12,500**, then **sixteen** numbered assumptions, including that the leave date sent was in the past and that the comparison was money-only because no ratings were supplied. Three separable answers rather than one feeling: `walkAwayCost`, `nextVest` and `offerHasToBeat`, with `verdict` **null** when no offer is given. Share links carry rounded bands rather than figures. US metros only, engine closed, one document per call, all recorded.

- [DocPin MCP - Publish an Agent's HTML to a Link You Control](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/docpin-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.docpin.app/mcp`, OAuth with dynamic client registration and PKCE, documented from the server's own contract because there is no API key to drive. A keyless `initialize` answers **401** naming its protected-resource document, and that document answers **200** with exactly **2** scopes, `publish` and `settings`, which is the split that decides what a connection can do. **The stable link is the entry:** republishing a `slug` puts a new version **behind the same link**, and around it sit the four capabilities nobody on the artifact shelf combines - `set_access` with `team`, `public`, `password`, `people` (emails and `@domains`) or `inherit`, version history with `restore_version`, `get_page_views` reporting **by whom** on a people-only page, and a per-page JSON store that `set_page_data` updates **without republishing**. Sharing a draft requires an `access` value, so the agent has to ask who should be allowed in. Page data is capped at **1 MB** and about **30 writes a minute**; upload links live **15 minutes** and take **25 MB**; drafts preview for about an hour and are not for sharing. **Free** is 3 pages, **Pro $8 a month** adds unlimited pages, custom domains and password or people-only pages.
- [AgentKeyGate MCP - A Pass Instead of the API Key](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/agentkeygate-mcp/) - self-hosted gateway, Apache-2.0, Node.js 22, Streamable HTTP at `https://{host}/mcp` behind a `gwa_...` agent token, **1.0.2** in the registry. **The agent never receives the service key:** it asks for a pass with a `ttl` and a call count and a reason up to **200** characters, a person approves in Telegram or on the web with those facts in view, and the pass `gwt_...` dies when the clock or the calls run out. **The data filter is why it earns the guide:** types and fields are chosen explicitly and everything else is cut from the JSON **before it reaches the agent**, `readOnly` is **on by default for CRM and support keys**, blocked writes do not consume quota, and `mask` replaces e-mails, separated phones, Luhn-valid cards and IBANs. The vendor's own example: a Bitrix24 lead returns seven fields and the agent gets `ID`, `STATUS_ID` and `OPPORTUNITY`. Weakening a filter needs a **fresh TOTP code** and shows a "was, now" page first. Recorded honestly: **0 stars**, created **2026-11-05**, single owner, no external audit, root on the server reads every key, filtering exists for four services, and the vendor's own `Checked live` column reads **`no`** on every client snippet including the **Hermes** one.

- [SumOffice MCP - Edit the Real xlsm and Get It Back](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/sumoffice-mcp/) - hosted remote server at `https://view.sumoffice.com/mcp`, `sumoffice-document` **0.3.0**, **21** tools, **no account and no key**, plus the same server as a Docker image for a local file over stdio. It opens a real `.docx`, `.xlsx` or `.xlsm` up to 50 MB in a private editor cabin, reads cells and formulas, the VBA project with its entry points and blockers, the Power Query steps and load targets, and the paragraphs, comments and tracked changes, proposes a change, applies it only on approval, and returns a copy as a 24-hour download link. **Driven on the read path:** the `cashflow` demo opened as a genuine `.xlsm` with three sheets, `vba_project: true`, two tables, one query table, one connection and `data_mashup: true`; `macro_list` returned `Module1.FlagCashGaps` user-runnable on the **native** route with no blockers and `Sheet1.Worksheet_Change` on the **excel-bridge** route blocked as an event-or-document module at line 12, without executing anything; `query_list` returned `MonthlyCashflow` with its load target and refresh state and **the M body withheld by engine policy with only its sha256 exposed**, which is the right call for the string that carries a connection credential. The round trip is the argument: the vendor's **20 September 2026** proof run opened an Enron workbook with a VBA project and a dynamic-array UDF, applied a proposed formula and saved a copy that Excel 16 opened with no repair dialog and `xl/vbaProject.bin` byte-identical. The write path refused twice in this session and both refusals are in the guide: `unsupported-cell-preview-edits` for plain numeric inputs, then `busy: all 5 editor cabins are in use`, the documented concurrency ceiling of the hosted server. It earns the entry beside the [Basis MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/basis-mcp/) engine catalogued the evening before: Basis recomputes and audits a workbook, SumOffice edits the file and ships the artifact back with its package parts intact.

**Provenance note worth keeping in the ledger.** This pass began on a catalogue clone three commits behind `origin/main`, which already carried that evening sweep and its two guides. Basis and CarbonMeld were therefore researched, probed and written up a second time, and the duplicate was caught only when the branch checkout refused because both guide directories already existed on the remote. - [ProveCart MCP - Agent Order Checks Before Payment](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/provecart-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://api.provecart.com/mcp`, keyless `initialize` **200** as `provecart` **1.0.2** with all **10** tools listed, and **the evidence tier stated rather than implied**: `provecart_scoreboard` and `provecart_certification_info` were called live and returned real payloads, while the three check tools refuse without an integrator key in the `X-API-Key` header and say so in one sentence, so the check payload is schema-read and not measured. `provecart_check_order`, `provecart_check_booking` and `provecart_check_reservation` compare what the agent built against the customer's own **mandate** and return a signed **MATCH**, **REVIEW** or **BLOCK** verdict before the payment is captured, with a non-MATCH answer carrying the Agent Correction Format - a `corrections` array of `dimension`, `action`, `expected`, `actual`, `reason`, a retry budget and a sealed evidence pointer. **The mandate is the part that makes this different from a prompt**: the order mandate carries **18** structured fields including `max_total_price`, `merchant_allowlist`, `merchant_blocklist`, `max_quantity`, `variant_constraints`, `price_basis`, `expires_at` and a `period_budget` with its own window, the booking mandate **26** including `airport_substitution`, `date_flex_days`, `fare_terms`, `max_connections`, `min_connection_minutes` and `max_layover_minutes`, and the reservation mandate **17** including `time_tolerance_minutes`, `party_size_max`, `max_deposit` and `cancellation`. The rules read live: **80** or above certifies, a pass is CURRENT for **90 days**, status is computed from the sealed record at read time, renewal is a newly generated exam, and a pass produces an Open Badges 3.0 / W3C Verifiable Credential under `did:web:api.provecart.com`. The limits are in the guide: it never holds or moves money, a verdict gates a payment only where the integrator's code calls the check first, the AI layer cannot overturn a block, business onboarding is a free **90-day** pilot rather than a published price, and `provecart.com` answers **401** to a plain reader-proxy fetch. - [lookfirst MCP - Human Approval Gate for Agent Writes](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/lookfirst-mcp/) - a local stdio MCP proxy, Apache-2.0 at `github.com/Aethelgard-Systems/lookfirst`, installed here from the repository and reporting `lookfirst 0.2.1` against a README that still says 0.2.0 pre-1.0. **Driven, not quoted:** the offline demo was run twice end to end. The approval run returned `{"status":"executed","approved_by":"elicitation:mcp","readback":"ok","readback_detail":"read-back matches","blocked":false}` and the fake bank balance moved **1,250.00 to 1,129.50 EUR** for a **120.50 EUR** transfer; the denial run returned `"status":"denied"` with the failed channel named and the balance untouched. Five behaviours are what earn the guide. **The decision fails closed and the default table is short**: `readOnlyHint` allows, `destructiveHint`, an unannotated write and an unknown tool all confirm, and an explicit rule beats the annotation while `deny` never executes. **The approval is bound to the arguments**: the webhook answer must carry the per-call HMAC token and echo `args_sha256` from the preview or it returns **403**, the web page binds its buttons the same way, and every channel shares one timeout where a timeout is a denial. **The write is verified by read-back** against `$args` and `$result` placeholders and reported as `ok`, `unklar` or `fehlgeschlagen`, with `structuredContent.lookfirst` carrying the verdict so a write is never reported as done on its own word. **The log is an Ed25519 hash chain**: `verify-log` walked the run to **OK, 20 signed and chained entries**, and the demo then rewrote the decision entry and the same command returned **TAMPERED, line 6, hash mismatch**, with the documented residual (end-truncation plus a deleted `.head` sidecar) closed by an external `--trusted-head` checkpoint. **The result is masked before the model sees it**: the agent received `[[IBAN_c30e2f3c...]]` and `[[NAME_5f082d93...]]`, passing the placeholder back works because the gate resolves it, and an invented one is refused with `Denied: unknown or expired placeholder`. The limits are the vendor's own and are in the guide: pre-1.0 with no field record, **0** stars, an autonomous client that auto-answers elicitation approves itself unless `confirm.elicitation` is off and the page is isolated at the network level, a separate OS user is not enough because every local user reaches loopback, the page has no login and is for `127.0.0.1`, an HTTP token is authentication rather than encryption, Windows is untested, and the mask is a deterministic pattern filter that misses split IBANs, zero-width text, Base64 secrets and keys like `db_password`. It earns a guide because [kosa8](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/kosa8-mcp/) isolates the server, TrustScan and AgentTrust judge an endpoint, and glc PromptGuard scores a prompt or an output, and **none of them stops one specific write at the argument level, names the human who approved it, verifies the result by reading it back and keeps a chain you can point at**.

Passive site-wide logging and active per-page submission receipts are different instruments, so both belong here. **A correction is recorded with the entry**: the guide's first version claimed the catalogue held the answer side of AI visibility and "the input side none", which was wrong, since IndexLinks has read verified crawler visits with timestamps since October 6 and the [AI Crawler Index](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/pathwren-ai-crawler-index/) verifies crawler IPs against operator-published ranges; the guide now names both and explains what this entry adds instead of asserting the slice was missing. The limits are in the guide: it measures rather than controls, the vendor's own framing is visit records and policy signals rather than rankings or model-training proof, the free plan is **1** site and **100** crawl visits a month with crawl analysis only, and `llms.txt` coverage, sitemap coverage, bot authenticity and the crawl-like-a-bot simulation all start at **Pro, $20 a month**.

The operator writes a mandate with a `purpose`, a `default` and an ordered clause list where each clause carries an `effect` of `permit`, `deny` or `escalate`; the agent passes the mandate plus the action it is about to take, and the first matching clause decides. Every answer carried a `hanria-receipt-v1` receipt with the mandate digest, the action digest, an issue time, a fifteen-minute window and a signature. `validate_mandate` reports the three failures that make a policy decorative, clauses that can never run because an earlier clause already decides them, unbounded prefixes and credential material, and it proved strict by refusing a first attempt that used `kind` values of `payment` and `access` and a free-text clause field, naming the offending field and the accepted taxonomy of `file`, `process`, `package`, `network`, `device`, `credential_use`, `transaction` and `administrative`. ## 🆕 November 2, 2026 - Midday Supplement (1 New, 1 Guide)

An hour after the midday pass, fired on the 11:00 MST tick, so this is a supplement rather than a second midday read: the window, the feed and the `/all` page were already dispositioned an hour earlier and are not re-argued here. What changed in the hour is three submissions (`Publish MCP` **#6621**, `norc` **#6622**, `Lingard Vocab` **#6623**) and one reversal with a reason attached.

- [AttriKit MCP - App Attribution That Returns a Decision](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/attrkit-mcp/) - stdio through `npx -y @attrkit/mcp`, published as **2.0.1** on npm with the MIT repository `KamyarTaher/attrikit-mcp` whose README carries the full **39**-tool table, the MCP setup page carrying the same inventory and count, and the pricing page carrying its free allowance in the headline. It is the first entry here that closes the loop from ad spend to app install to subscription revenue to a budget decision. `get_campaign_decision` returns the attribution engine's call verbatim and the vendor states the model reports it rather than recomputing it; `record_campaign_decision` stores the scale, cut or hold call with the inputs that produced it, so the call can be graded later once enough results exist, with the vendor's own caveat that a suggestion is not a profit guarantee. Spend is an input rather than a copied dashboard: `import_spend` takes ad level CSV rows with the paired `adset_id`/`ad_id` rule enforced client side since 1.0.0, `pull_network_spend` reads an authorized ad account, `set_cost_model` records allocation, and `get_spend` returns it beside installs and events. RevenueCat joins purchases, renewals and refunds to installs. The delivery rules, the timeouts (15 seconds on most tools, 120 on `export_events`, `import_spend` and `pull_network_spend`), the version 1 export cut at the newest 100,000 events, the one-member workspace, the web SDK not yet on npm and the 25-month retention are all in the guide, as is the pricing read directly: first **10,000** qualified installs free once with no card, then **$249** a month including 10,000, then **$0.015** each, which prices 50,000 at **$849** and 100,000 at **$1,599**. It earns a guide because [Mobzio MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/mobzio-mcp/) answers which link produced a marketplace order for a Russian and CIS seller and stops there, while the ad surfaces here stop at the creative ([Abyssale MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/abyssale-mcp/), [AdTest.AI MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/adtest-mcp/), [Ad Library Intelligence MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/ad-library-intelligence-mcp/), [Adspy MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/adspy-mcp/), [AdMake AI MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/admake-ai-mcp/)), so no entry in **1,085** guides joined spend to installs and returned a decision with its inputs saved.

**Reversal, stated plainly.** The midday pass an hour earlier grouped `AttriKit` (`#6592`) with developer tooling and mobile attribution and held it there. That grouping is reversed here on the surface rather than on the vendor: mobile attribution had no catalogued class to be held against (`WarpLink` was listed as identified and never written up, and [Mobzio MCP](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/mobzio-mcp/) is marketplace deeplinks for one regional seller set), and the decision and spend tools are an operator surface, not a developer one.
