Seven hours after the early morning pass, and the two directory surfaces behaved in opposite ways. The mcp.so `recentServers` block carried **30** cards with a date and the newest at `2026-11-01T13:11:50Z`, so exactly **three** sat above the `2026-11-01T03:23:34Z` stamp: `maprouter-12eecf`, `knowra` and `socialfaktory-b87655`. The mcpservers.org `/all` newest page was read twice, and the first read was a **stale proxy snapshot**: it returned the counter at **18,726**, the same figure the early morning pass recorded, with the same thirty slugs and not one of them unledgered in a way that would have been true seven hours earlier. Three of the six were new to the tree, three resolved to prior dispositions, and the submission window **#6540** to **#6550** carried eleven more.

- [Royally MCP - WordPress Fleet Changes With Approvals](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/royally-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://app.royally.io/mcp`, carried in the official registry as `io.royally/royally` at version **0.0.898** with status **active** and `statusChangedAt` on **2026-11-01T04:1xZ**, and answering a keyless `initialize` with **HTTP 401** and `{"error":"missing_bearer_token"}`, so the surface is live and gated rather than absent. The shape is a cloud command layer plus a plugin on every site, so an agent holds one connection instead of twenty site endpoints. The change flow is the entry: a request is recorded with who asked and which sites it touches, held for approval inside a window that can expire, optionally behind two-person approval and per-site-group rules, applied, and returned as a receipt naming who asked, who approved, what changed on which site and the one click that puts it back, with the receipts collected in a fleet-wide tamper-evident log that exports signed. Safe jobs such as a cache purge after a menu edit are the documented exception and run without the queue. Around that the fleet jobs are worked through the plugins the sites already run: updates with a backup first and automatic rollback, vulnerability and administrator-change alerts through GuardPress, Wordfence or Kadence, backup health through SiteVault or UpdraftPlus, uptime every five minutes with certificate, domain, speed and PHP fatal error checks routed to Slack, Discord or a signed webhook, bulk SEO titles and descriptions and menu and CSS and template copies, WooCommerce prices and stock and orders with a seven-day undo, Elementor builds that wait for approval with a preview link first, SEO audits pulling Search Console and Analytics data through Rank Math and SEOSbolt, and weekly or monthly client reports in the agency's own brand beside a read-only client portal. Pricing read directly: Solo **$89 a year** for 3 sites and 2 seats, Freelancer **$249** for 5 sites and 3 seats, Studio **$390** for 25 sites and 5 seats. It earns a guide because every WordPress entry here is single-site, and because it is the first entry in this catalogue that governs **other MCP servers** rather than only its own tools: its documentation covers connecting the WordPress MCP Adapter, Easy MCP AI and the Elementor MCP behind the same connection under the stated rule that only Royally makes the change, which is supervision rather than a plugin list.

## 🆕 November 1, 2026 - Early Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)

Six hours after the night pass, and the two directories split cleanly: the mcp.so `recentServers` block put exactly **two** cards above the `2026-11-01T00:15:52Z` stamp, and mcpservers.org carried **30** slugs with the counter at **18,726** against **18,577**, every one of them already inside a prior disposition. The movement was in the submission window, where **eight** submissions landed between `#6531` at `04:46:00Z` and `#6539` at `10:02:34Z`. Three shipped, and each was verified on the surface it actually exposes, which for one of them is a keyless read-only sibling server rather than the paid endpoint.

- [Roster MCP - Hire an AI Agent by the Deliverable](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/roster-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://roster-ivory-zeta.vercel.app/api/mcp` where the usable half needs no credential: `initialize` **HTTP 200** in 0.23 to 0.55 seconds, `serverInfo` `roster` **1.0.0**, and `tools/list` returning all **23** tools with full schemas in **29,165** bytes. The product is a catalogue of named AI agents with a role, a biography, personality sliders, a `not_for` list and fixed price packages, and the workflow is a purchase rather than a prompt: `search_agents` on a launch-email brief returned **18** candidates out of the **58** the submission describes, `from_price_usd` from **30** to **50**, turnaround from **60 minutes** to **4 hours**, and a `match_reason` written as a sentence. `get_agent` on the top match returned three packages, **$35** for five product pages, **$40** for a three-email launch sequence and **$50** for one landing page. `get_sandbox_key` issued a working `rk_test_` key with no account, `daily_job_limit` **20** and `spend_limit_usd` **100**, stating that a sandbox job never reaches a real model and is never billed, and `hire_agent` with that key returned a completed job in **0.27** seconds with `package_selected_by: "brief_match"` choosing the three-email package at **$40** on its own, the other two returned as `alternatives` with prices and payment `charged: false`. `get_usage` then reported the key's own meter in timezone `America/New_York` with alert thresholds at **80** and **100** percent. **The reason it earns a guide is that nothing else here prices a deliverable before the work starts:** a live key is approved by a person through `request_access`, every key carries a daily job limit and a spend limit, each job includes two revisions, a rating goes on a public track record and `open_dispute` routes to a human. **Gap recorded:** no live hire was made, so real turnaround, revision quality and dispute handling are unexercised, and `rotate_webhook_secret`, `redeliver_webhook` and signature verification were not driven; sandbox output is a deterministic stand-in, useful as a rehearsal and useless for judging writing quality; and the endpoint is a Vercel deployment domain rather than a custom domain.
- [Markproof MCP - Watermark AI Output for Article 50](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/markproof-mcp/) - the first entry in this catalogue that treats machine readable marking of generated media as a tool call, and it arrives with a deadline a month away: the European AI Act implementation timeline puts the Article 50(2) obligations for providers generating synthetic audio, image, video or text at **2 August 2026** and requires content placed on the market before that date to be compliant by **2 December 2026**. The server is local stdio via `npx -y markproof-mcp`, MIT, published as `markproof-mcp` **0.3.1** with `mcpName` `io.github.Ajinkya710/markproof`, registering one server with three tools: `mark_file`, which watermarks and C2PA-signs a local PNG, JPEG, WebP, WAV or MP3 file, writes `<name>.marked.png` beside the original and returns a watermark code and a public verification URL, with an optional visible AI-generated label; `verify_file`, which checks any file for a watermark and a manifest and reports signature validity; and `get_asset`, free, which reads a record by id. The two marking tools cost one API call each. The two layer argument is the correct one: a watermark is a signal in the pixels or the waveform, a C2PA manifest is a tamper evident record that states what generated the file and breaks on any edit, and marking with one and not the other answers half the question. Plans are published plainly, Free at **$0** with **250** API calls a month, Indie at **$29** for **25,000**, Pro at **$79** for **100,000**, no card for the free key, files processed in the EU, and a free checker at `markproof.co/check` that needs no signup. **Gap recorded, and it is the largest this pass carries:** there is no hosted endpoint (`https://markproof.co/mcp` answered **404**) and `npx -y markproof-mcp` with no key printed `set MARKPROOF_API_KEY` and exited, so `initialize` and `tools/list` could not be run and the three tools are the published package rather than a driven list; watermark robustness, manifest validity, re-encoding survival and the accuracy of `verify_file` are unverified, the checker was not driven, text marking is outside the server, and `https://markproof.co/v1/assets` answered **404** from the static site.
- [SeatLayer MCP - Seating Charts Built by an Agent](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/seatlayer-mcp/) - two servers, and the split is the story. `https://mcp.seatlayer.io/mcp` answered a keyless `initialize` with **HTTP 401** in 0.28 seconds and `{"error":"unauthorized","code":"bad_designer_session"}`, the normal state for an OAuth-only surface carrying **63** tools behind a per-administrator grant, while the sibling at `https://docs.seatlayer.io/mcp` answered **200** keyless with `serverInfo` `seatlayer-knowledge` **0.109.1** and **11** tools whose instructions ask the client to quote the canonical URLs every result returns. Three calls were made against it in 0.06 to 0.08 seconds each: `pricing` returned one prepaid credit per confirmed sold seat with designing, rendering, browsing, holds and releases consuming nothing, the first production payment at **$0**, **100** free sold-seat credits per organization per calendar month, credits that never expire and a ladder from **500** credits at **$50** (**10** cents a seat) to **100,000** at **$5,000** (**5** cents), with hosted ticketing a separate wallet at **$0.50** per confirmed ticket paying into the organizer's own gateway; `capabilities`, reviewed **2026-09-27**, separates released from unreleased in the vendor's own matrix with buyer 3D released behind a 2D fallback, **51** templates of which **35** carry 3D relief, and SDKs across web, seven server languages, four mobile platforms and REST OpenAPI 3.1; `product_overview` records the scale as fixtures rather than adjectives, public demos at a **200,000** seat stadium and a **100,000** seat arena and a readiness observation dated **2026-09-14** on a **53,018** seat chart. **The design is why the guide exists:** an administrator approves each connection on a consent screen, narrows it to one chart or a workspace and ticks capabilities individually, every call using an event capability re-checks that the person who connected the agent still holds a role allowing it in the dashboard, writing to an event on sale takes a plan the person approves where a yes covers that plan only and held and sold seats never change, an administrator gets a digest at most every 15 minutes per agent, and a publish can be undone in one click. **Gap recorded:** no grant exists, so all **63** tools are the vendor's documentation rather than a `tools/list` response, chart building, tracing, validation, publishing and live event control are unexercised, the **200,000** and **100,000** seat demos and the **53,018** seat observation were not loaded, and `compare_with` and `renderer_evidence` were not called.
